Assume air behaves as a perfect gas with gamma = 1.4 and R = 287 J/(kg·K).
Treat the nozzle flow as isentropic since it is frictionless (no shocks, adiabatic).
Given inlet Mach number M1 = 2.0 and area ratio A2/A1 = 0.7.
Compute the inlet area ratio A1/A* using the isentropic area-Mach relation for M1 = 2.0.
Determine the exit area ratio A2/A* from A2/A1 times A1/A*.
Obtain the exit Mach number M2 from the isentropic area-Mach relation, selecting the supersonic branch because the inlet flow is supersonic.
Compute static temperatures T1 and T2 from the total temperature using T0/T = 1 + 0.2·M^2, with T0 constant (isentropic).
Compute inlet velocity V1 = M1·sqrt(gamma·R·T1) and exit velocity V2 = M2·sqrt(gamma·R·T2).
Report the change in exit velocity relative to the inlet velocity, noting whether it is an increase or decrease, as a percentage of V1.
Show all intermediate values (A1/A*, A2/A*, M2, T1, T2, V1, V2) in the solution.
